dedupe_keys.name: umi urban modeling interface mit sustainable design lab

description: umi, the Urban Modeling Interface, is a multi-year effort of MIT's Sustainable Design Lab to evaluate the environmental performance of neighbourhoods and cities. It runs as a design environment inside Rhinoceros 3D on massing models and has an API for adding performance modules. Modules report site statistics and calculate neighbourhood daylight access, operational energy based on EnergyPlus, walkability to user-chosen amenities, embodied energy and carbon over many years, local food production, and an optimal mix of district energy supply systems. Files can be built in Rhino or through the UBEM.io web app, which also compares umi results. Coverage: any neighbourhood modelled in Rhino. Access: free download of the current version for Rhino 8, a legacy version for Rhino 7 and a pre-release. Licence: not stated. Caveats: it needs Rhino 8 on Windows, and massing-level inputs simplify real buildings. Simulation uses: comparing urban design options for energy, daylight, walkability and carbon. Related records: EnergyPlus, CitySim and CityBES.
